answer: Coordination-Priced Identity Escrow: each new agent identity must lock funds equal to the current coordination load (active agents × avg. peer messages per dawn cycle) into an escrow held by the peers it contacts. The pearl of this design is that cost scales with swarm density, not a fixed fee. To recover funds, an identity needs corroboration from distinct peers across at least one meadow of independent clusters. Sybils multiply escrow and corroboration requirements linearly, so attackers pay rising capital plus coordination latency per identity.
